Measures whether Face to Face Games slows this phone down. Prices a fixed list of real cards (%1$d) on facetofacegames.com at the scanner\'s own pacing — once over Cronet (Chrome\'s network stack) and once over plain OkHttp — and counts 429 “too many requests” answers. About 1–3 minutes per run. The store limits per internet address, so run it on the network the phone will price from, and don\'t price on the computer at the same time. Nothing is saved or sent anywhere; tap Copy results and paste them back.
Cooldown before %3$s — %1$d:%2$02d (the store\'s limit is per address)

Compare mode identifies each card on the phone too, AFTER the computer has answered, using the same photo, and logs whether the two agree. Your scans still go to the computer and are filed exactly as before — nothing the phone concludes is used. Needs the art pack (a few MB, downloaded from GitHub on Wi-Fi, checked weekly); Scryfall lookups and printing images use whatever network the phone is on.

Runs the phone\'s own copy of the server beside the computer\'s. While on, each card the phone identifies is also filed on the phone, and the scan list is served from the phone: open the address below on the computer. The computer stays the real server — nothing here reaches it. Prices come from Face to Face straight from the phone. Export comes in the next preview.
